episode.title: What If 10 Business Titans Went Broke? Five Years to Prove It Wasn't Luck
episode.notes: writers' room stages 1-2 (story, scenes, lines); beats, performance, edit, voices and Shorts follow on these frozen words after the creator's approval of the script

voice.style: a warm, quick, slightly wry storyteller with a low voice, curious and never solemn

world.host: a caricatured present-day New York: courthouse, highway motel, garages, warehouses

musk.card: Elon Musk as our caricature: tall, broad shoulders, short dark hair, tired eyes, black T-shirt, grease on his hands

belfort.card: Jordan Belfort as our caricature: compact, slicked hair, wide grin, a sharp suit that has seen better days

oleary.card: Kevin O'Leary as our caricature: bald, round glasses, dark suit, a calm half-smile

trump.card: Donald Trump as our caricature: swept blond hair, long red tie, navy suit, a phone held at arm's length

kiyosaki.card: Robert Kiyosaki as our caricature: grey hair, tanned, open-collar shirt, a pointing finger

cuban.card: Mark Cuban as our caricature: dark hair, T-shirt and jeans, arms crossed, a warehouse office with no chairs

cardone.card: Grant Cardone as our caricature: bald, trim beard, tight suit, a phone pressed to his ear

hormozi.card: Alex Hormozi as our caricature: very muscular, shaved head, beard, a tight black T-shirt

zuckerberg.card: Mark Zuckerberg as our caricature: short curly hair, grey T-shirt, a laptop in a public library

bezos.card: Jeff Bezos as our caricature: bald, bright smile, a quilted vest, reading a report

vance.card: Vance, an invented buyer of failing companies: grey suit, grey tie, grey smile

drama.premise: Ten famous business titans go bankrupt on one Monday, lose every lender, and keep only their skills.
drama.question: Was their money ever skill, or was it luck?
drama.promise: five years of their comeback, who rises, who stays down, and who quietly wins

musk.need: trust someone to speak for him
musk.flaw: says the truth too quietly, then gives in
musk.change: says 'probably not' out loud and pays for it

belfort.change: refuses the cover-up and sells the truth

kiyosaki.flaw: keeps his theory when the world changes
kiyosaki.change: none: still preaching in the lobby

oleary.want: the best return on forty dollars

bezos.flaw: only buys what he has read

loops.question: who makes the best deal of the five years, for forty dollars?
how do you make money when nobody lends to you?
will Belfort keep his promise not to promise?
will Cardone ever get a yes?
can they build five hundred in time?
what will the leftover cells do?
what will Cuban do with the truth?

setups.what: O'Leary's thick stack of white envelopes
'Me? Never.' Belfort promises not to promise
three hundred leftover cheap cells on the shelf

ending.note: O'Leary owned a slice of eight of them; the verdict closes skill or luck

lines.text: Monday, nine in the morning. A courthouse hallway in New York, and one long wooden bench.
Ten men sit on it, shoulder to shoulder, and none of them looks at the others.
Donald Trump fixes his tie in the black screen of his phone. Robert Kiyosaki is telling the guard that debt is a gift.
On Friday they owned towers, rockets, studios and stores. By lunch, a clerk will turn all of it into paperwork.
But nobody will lend them a dollar after today. Not a bank, not a friend, not the man beside them.
They walk out with one thing: whatever is inside their heads.
You'd think that's enough to start again. Five years will show if it was ever skill.
And the best deal of those five years is about to be made on this bench, for forty dollars.

drama.stakes: ten fortunes and the proof of who earned them

lines.text: At the far end, Kevin O'Leary reads the others one by one, the way a man reads price tags.
Then he slides along the bench to Elon Musk.
You can still build things?
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: I can build anything. That isn't the problem.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: So what is?
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: Nobody pays for the parts before the thing exists.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Then I will. Forty dollars.
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: Forty dollars buys one wheel.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: And ten percent of everything you ever build. Forever.
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: Ten percent for forty? I've sold air for more.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: Then sell me some. I've got an envelope for you too.
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: Why would I sign that?
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Because forty is more than anyone else in this building is offering.
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: Musk signs. O'Leary moves one seat along and holds out the next envelope to Jordan Belfort.
Forever is a long word in a contract.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: It's a short one in a bankruptcy.
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: Belfort reads it to the last line, folds it, and hands it back. O'Leary stands, a thick stack of white envelopes under his arm.

drama.stakes: Musk sells a piece of his whole future for one wheel

scene.place: the bankruptcy court hallway, the long bench
scene.why_now: the clerk has just taken their fortunes; nobody will lend them again
scene.want: money for parts without giving away control
scene.obstacle_want: a slice of everything Musk will ever build
scene.turn: Musk signs away ten percent of his future for one wheel
scene.real_subject: who owns the next five years

lines.text: By noon the ten are back on the street, and the city teaches them its first lesson.
Grant Cardone asks a bank for a small loan. The banker types his name, reads the screen, and slides the form back.
Robert Kiyosaki asks for a credit card. Same screen. Same slide.
Donald Trump taps his card at a coffee cart, and the machine beeps twice.
Here's what you learn fast on that street. A loan was only ever a stranger's trust with interest on top. And nobody trusts them for a cent.
So the only money they can touch is money they make today, with their hands or with their mouths.
Musk has forty dollars and a parts list. Jordan Belfort has a phone with no numbers in it.

drama.stakes: without credit, every plan must pay on the first day

lines.text: A week later, a supermarket parking lot. Musk has built one good scooter out of three broken ones.
For six hours he has explained its battery to everyone who walks by. Nobody stops.
Belfort watches from the curb with a hot dog. Then he takes the handlebars without asking.
He never mentions the battery. He lets a delivery rider take one free lap of the lot, then names three times Musk's price.
The rider pays cash.
You were selling a battery. I sold him an hour of his evening.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: It's the same scooter.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Not to him. He rode it before he paid.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: So you gave it away first.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Give a little first. People hate owing you.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: What do you want?
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Half. You build, I sell.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: Ten percent already belongs to a man with envelopes.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Then forty-five each. I won't even ask.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: One rule. You never promise what I haven't built.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Me? Never.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: They shake hands. Neither of them lets go first.

drama.stakes: Musk's skill is worth nothing until somebody pays for it

scene.place: a supermarket parking lot, late afternoon
scene.why_now: Belfort has just sold in thirty seconds what Musk could not sell in six hours
scene.want: a seller who never lies about his machines
scene.obstacle_want: half the business and the freedom to sell his own way
scene.turn: the free lap sells the scooter and Musk has to take a partner
scene.real_subject: whether a liar can be trusted

lines.text: Across the river, a motel by the highway rents rooms by the week. Two men split the cheapest one.
Debt is how the rich get richer. Write that down.
lines.speaker: kiyosaki

lines.text: Fantastic. Lend me some.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: I don't have any.
lines.speaker: kiyosaki

lines.text: Then you don't own the thing you're selling.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: Banks forget. In a year they'll beg to lend us.
lines.speaker: kiyosaki

lines.text: My companies went to bankruptcy court six times. The banks never came back first.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: So who did?
lines.speaker: kiyosaki

lines.text: The cameras.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: Cameras don't pay rent.
lines.speaker: kiyosaki

lines.text: Watch.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: Trump props his phone on a plastic chair by the empty pool and goes live.
Eleven strangers watch him eat a vending machine sandwich with a knife and fork, like a state dinner.
By midnight, eleven is four thousand. Kiyosaki calls the bank again and gets the voicemail.

drama.stakes: two men whose money always came from others now have no others

scene.place: a cheap highway motel room, then the empty pool
scene.why_now: the motel wants the week's rent tomorrow
scene.want: a lender who believes in his plan
scene.turn: Trump stops asking for money and starts asking for attention
scene.real_subject: whose skill still works without a bank

lines.text: Six months later, the garage behind the motel smells of solder.
Musk sleeps on a folding cot beside the workbench and rebuilds thirty scooters a month. Every one leaves with Belfort.
Belfort never says lithium. If you deliver food for a living, he sells you one more delivery an hour.
Across town, Alex Hormozi walks into dying gyms and offers to fill them. He gets paid only from new members, cash first.
Mark Zuckerberg sits in a public library writing code that finds broken shop websites. Then he fixes them for a fee.
Mark Cuban rents one bicycle to a kid who delivers lunch. Then two bicycles. Then twenty.
Jeff Bezos sells used books off a folding table and writes down every title that sells twice.
But Grant Cardone, making a hundred calls a day, gets a hundred hang-ups.
His plan pools other people's money into a building. And the one thing his name can't raise anymore is their trust.

drama.stakes: the skills that need trust stall while the others earn

lines.text: By month nine, a hundred thousand people tune in every night to watch Trump eat cereal from a crystal glass.
One night, Kiyosaki steps into the frame.
Mind if I teach them something useful?
lines.speaker: kiyosaki

lines.text: Two minutes. They come for me, not homework.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: Lesson one. Your house is not an asset.
lines.speaker: kiyosaki

lines.text: You're losing them. Nine hundred gone. Two thousand.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: They need to hear this.
lines.speaker: kiyosaki

lines.text: They need to hear me.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: Trump turns the phone. Kiyosaki is out of the picture, and the count climbs back in seconds.

drama.stakes: Kiyosaki loses the one stage he still has

scene.place: the motel pool at night, on a live video
scene.why_now: Trump's audience has grown past anything Kiyosaki can reach alone
scene.turn: the count falls while Kiyosaki teaches and Trump takes the phone back
scene.real_subject: who the crowd actually came for

lines.text: Year one. Mark Cuban runs two hundred delivery riders out of a warehouse office with no chairs.
He has heard about the scooters that never break down.
How many can you make by Christmas?
lines.speaker: cuban

lines.text: Fifty. Fifty good ones.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Five hundred.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: We have parts for fifty.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: He's modest. It's a condition.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: Five hundred by the twentieth of December, or you never walk in here again.
lines.speaker: cuban

lines.text: Can you?
lines.speaker: cuban

lines.text: Yes.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Cuban signs. It is the biggest order either of them has seen in a year.

drama.stakes: the order that saves them leaves no room for a single mistake

scene.why_now: Cuban needs scooters before the holiday rush
scene.want: an order he can build without cutting corners
scene.obstacle_want: the biggest order Cuban will sign today
scene.turn: Musk says yes to a number he knows he cannot build safely
scene.real_subject: who decides what is true about the machines

lines.text: In the parking lot, Musk doesn't start the van.
You promised what I haven't built.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: You said yes. I heard you.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: Because you'd already said it.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: That's how big orders work. Promise, then build.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: That's how fires work.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Belfort laughs. Then he sees Musk isn't laughing, and stops.
For eleven weeks the garage lights never go off.
The good cells won't arrive before Christmas, so Musk orders cheap ones from a seller he has never met.
A heat test takes a day per batch. He skips it on the last two hundred.
On the nineteenth of December, five hundred scooters roll into Cuban's warehouse. One day early.
Cuban pays. Belfort frames the receipt. Three hundred cheap cells are left over on a garage shelf.

drama.stakes: two hundred riders now carry an untested battery

scene.place: the van in Cuban's parking lot
scene.why_now: Musk has just promised five hundred because Belfort already had
scene.want: Belfort to admit the promise was a lie
scene.obstacle_want: keep the order and the money
scene.turn: Musk names the danger and then builds the five hundred anyway
scene.real_subject: the safety margin they just gave away

lines.text: Year two. A black car waits outside the motel office.
A network wants a show. How to Lose a Billion. Season one.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: And what will you own, exactly?
lines.speaker: kiyosaki

lines.text: The audience. The rest is paperwork.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: An audience isn't an asset.
lines.speaker: kiyosaki

lines.text: It paid for this car.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: A car is a liability.
lines.speaker: kiyosaki

lines.text: Not when somebody else pays for it.
lines.speaker: trump

lines.text: The car pulls away. Kiyosaki carries his bag to an old Toyota at the far end of the lot.
He slept in one once, a long time ago, with Kim. He still knows which seat folds flat.

drama.stakes: Kiyosaki is back where he started forty years ago

scene.place: the motel parking lot, beside a black car
scene.why_now: the network's car has come for Trump
scene.want: prove Trump's new money isn't real wealth
scene.obstacle_want: leave with the car and the contract
scene.turn: Trump turns Kiyosaki's own rule against him and drives off

lines.text: Year three. Two in the morning. The garage behind the motel is dark.
On the shelf, one of the three hundred leftover cells starts to hiss.
By the time the fire trucks arrive, the garage is a black box without a roof. Nobody is hurt. Everything else is gone.
Those cells came from the same box as Cuban's.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Cuban's have run for two years. They're fine.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: Two hundred of them never had the heat test.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: You never told me that.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: I told you we had parts for fifty.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: You said it quietly.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: You never listen when it's quiet.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: If Cuban hears this, we're finished.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: If a rider's scooter burns, we're worse than finished.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Belfort looks at the black shelf for a long time. He doesn't answer.
Replacing two hundred batteries would cost more than they have left.

drama.stakes: two hundred riders, and every dollar they have

scene.place: the burnt-out garage at dawn, ash on everything
scene.why_now: the leftover cheap cells just burned the garage down
scene.want: keep the fire away from Cuban
scene.obstacle_want: tell Cuban and pull the untested batteries
scene.turn: Musk admits the two hundred were never tested
scene.surface_topic: the box the cells came from

lines.text: Two days later, a man in a grey suit steps over the ashes. His name is Vance, and he buys companies before their bad week.
I'll buy the company today. You're both rich by Friday.
lines.speaker: vance

lines.text: What's the catch?
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: The fire was old wiring in an old garage. Nothing to do with batteries.
lines.speaker: vance

lines.text: Two hundred riders are sitting on those batteries.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: And they'll be fine. Probably.
lines.speaker: vance

lines.text: You know how this kind of paper works.
lines.speaker: vance

lines.text: I signed paper like that once. I paid for it in a cell.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: Then you know it works.
lines.speaker: vance

lines.text: That's why I'm not signing.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: Vance leaves his card on the burnt workbench.
Belfort picks up his phone and does something he has never done in a sale. He calls the buyer to tell him what's wrong.

drama.stakes: a fortune by Friday against two hundred riders

scene.place: the burnt garage, two days later
scene.why_now: they are broke, and a buyer has arrived with cash
scene.want: a way out that does not end in a cell
scene.obstacle_want: buy the company before the truth gets out
scene.turn: Belfort recognises the paper from his old life and refuses it

lines.text: The next morning, Cuban's warehouse. Two hundred scooters stand in rows.
Two hundred of your batteries skipped a test. We want them back.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: Are they bad?
lines.speaker: cuban

lines.text: Probably not. I don't sell probably.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Who pays for two hundred new ones?
lines.speaker: cuban

lines.text: We do.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: With what?
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: With everything. I did it once before, on a Christmas Eve.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Nobody has ever come in here to give me money back.
lines.speaker: cuban

lines.text: Belfort opens his mouth to make a pitch. For once, he closes it.
Fix them. Then bring me next year's number. A real one.
lines.speaker: cuban

lines.text: They spend every dollar on two hundred new batteries, and Musk tests each one twice, on camera.
For three months they eat from the motel vending machine. Belfort calls it the executive menu.

drama.stakes: they give up all their cash to keep one customer's trust

scene.place: Cuban's warehouse, between rows of scooters
scene.want: keep Cuban as a customer after the truth
scene.obstacle_want: never be lied to by a supplier
scene.turn: the recall they pay for wins the next order
scene.real_subject: what trust is worth in money

lines.text: Year five. Cuban's riders run on five thousand of their batteries, and not one has burned.
Belfort's whole pitch is one sentence now. Ours burned once. That's why they don't.
Grant Cardone works their phones. Same calls as year one. Now people pick up, because the name on the box means something.
Hormozi runs sixty gyms on cash. Zuckerberg sold his little website robot and vanished into a bigger one.
Trump is filming season four of How to Lose a Billion, and every season he loses it more profitably.
And Kiyosaki is in the motel lobby, explaining to the night clerk why debt is a gift. The clerk has heard it before.
Then a buyer walks in who has read every page of the fire report.
I read your fire report. All of it.
lines.speaker: bezos

lines.text: Most buyers ask us to bury it.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: That's why I'm offering double what they would.
lines.speaker: bezos

lines.text: Double.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Make it a partnership, and you can buy lunch.
lines.speaker: belfort

drama.stakes: five years of choices are priced at last

scene.place: the new factory office, a framed receipt on the wall
scene.why_now: the fire report is public and buyers are calling
scene.obstacle_want: own the company that told the truth
scene.turn: the report they could have buried doubles their price

lines.text: Five years after the bench, Musk and Belfort walk into the same courthouse to register the deal.
The bench is still there. So is Kevin O'Leary.
Ten percent. Remember?
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: Of a burnt garage?
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Of everything. Fires included. Read the envelope.
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: You got lucky with him.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: I didn't pick him.
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: Belfort's grin stays on a second too long.
He opens his briefcase. Eight signed envelopes. Trump. Kiyosaki. Cardone. Hormozi. Cuban. Bezos. Zuckerberg. Musk.
Eight?
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: Nine offered. One man read to the last line and said no.
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: I read contracts.
lines.speaker: belfort

lines.text: Then you went into business with a man who doesn't.
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: Musk looks at the floor. Belfort looks at Musk.
Most of these paid back my forty. Three of them paid for everything.
lines.speaker: oleary

lines.text: So it was luck.
lines.speaker: musk

lines.text: Luck chose the three. I made sure I owned all eight.
lines.speaker: oleary

drama.stakes: who really won the five years

scene.place: the courthouse hallway, the same bench
scene.why_now: the deal must be registered in this building
scene.want: walk past the bench owing nothing
scene.obstacle_want: collect ten percent of the best company on the street
scene.turn: O'Leary opens the briefcase and every envelope is there

lines.text: Ten men walked out of this building with nothing but what they knew.
The ones whose skill ran on other people's trust waited years for it. Some are still waiting.
The ones who could build or sell with their own hands were back within months.
And the one who never built or sold anything spread forty dollars across eight of them.
Luck decided which envelope paid. Skill decided who was still standing when it did.
So if you sat on that bench tomorrow, which envelope would be yours?

drama.stakes: the answer to skill or luck
